belief: If this treatment didn't work, nothing will.
origins: After a treatment fails, hope takes a hit. Repeated disappointment trains us to expect failure and to stop trying. Fatigue and cost add to the temptation to quit.
teaches: Peter and his friends had fished all night and caught nothing. Jesus said, “Put out into deep water, and let down your nets for a catch,” and Peter said, “Because You say so, I will let down the nets” (Luke 5:4–5). Scripture encourages persistence: “Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up” (Galatians 6:9). One failed treatment does not mean all will fail, and God’s purposes are bigger than any plan.
self_statements: It did not work, so nothing will.
I am wasting time and money.
I am tired of being disappointed.
errors: Believing a treatment either works or nothing will.
Predicting that all options will fail.
Feeling disappointed and concluding there is no hope.
questions: What exactly did not work, and what did we learn from it?
What does my doctor say about next steps?
How do I care for my heart after disappointment?
Who can support me through the next try?
truth: One failed treatment is one failed treatment. I can grieve the disappointment, ask my doctor about other options, and keep trusting God, who is with me whether or not the next step works.
hw_truths: Failure of one is not failure of all.
I can ask my doctor about next steps.
I do not despise small beginnings.
God is with me either way.
log: Each week, note one step you took toward the next option.
actions: Take time to recover from disappointment.
prayer: Lord, I am discouraged by treatment that did not work. Give me courage, wisdom about next steps, and hope in You. Amen.
